report.tagline: The world's biggest online store and marketplace, tied together by Prime fast delivery, a huge ads business and AWS cloud computing.
report.simpleSummary: Amazon is a website and app where you can buy almost anything and get it fast, often the next day. About 60% of items are sold by outside sellers, and Amazon takes a cut and charges them for storage, delivery and ads. Prime members pay a yearly fee for free fast delivery and Prime Video. Amazon also rents computing power to other companies through AWS, which makes most of its profit.

overview.whatItDoes: Amazon runs an online store where it sells its own stock and lets millions of outside sellers list products. It offers fast delivery through its own warehouses and drivers, Prime membership, ads for sellers and brands, and many other services like Prime Video, Alexa and AWS. Its store is built to win on selection, low prices and convenience.
howItWorks: Shoppers search or ask the AI assistant (now Alexa for Shopping, earlier Rufus) and buy with one click.
Outside sellers list items and pay a referral fee, often about 15% of the price.
Many sellers use Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA): they ship stock to Amazon warehouses and Amazon packs and delivers it for a fee.
Sellers and brands pay for sponsored ads to appear at the top of search results.
Prime members pay $14.99 a month or $139 a year in the US for fast free delivery, video, music and deals.
AWS sells cloud computing, storage and AI services to businesses.
overview.valueProposition: For shoppers: the biggest selection at low prices, delivered fast, with easy returns. For sellers: access to hundreds of millions of shoppers and Amazon's delivery network. For Amazon: each part feeds the others, the famous flywheel.

businessModel.summary: Amazon makes money from its own sales, seller fees, ads, subscriptions like Prime and AWS. The store has thin margins; ads and AWS make most of the profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Referral fees (often about 15%), FBA fulfilment fees and storage.
Sponsored products, brands and Prime Video ads; about $20 billion a quarter (estimate), growing about 12%.
Prime, Music, Kindle Unlimited and others.

businessModel.pricing: Prime (US): $14.99 a month or $139 a year. Seller referral fee: typically 8% to 15% by category. FBA fees vary by size and weight. Professional seller plan: $39.99 a month.
costDrivers: AI data centres and AWS hardware ($220 billion capex in 2026)
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $30 item sold by a third-party seller using FBA, Amazon might keep about $4.50 as a referral fee and $5 to $6 in FBA fees, and the seller may spend another $2 to $3 on ads. So Amazon earns $11 to $13 on that sale while costs to store and deliver it are maybe $6 to $8. Ads are almost pure profit. North America retail makes about 7.7 cents of operating profit per dollar of sales, while AWS makes about 39 cents.

howTheyGetUsers: Being the first place many people search for products

whatBringsUsersBack: Prime fee already paid, so people buy more to get value

growth.moat: Amazon's moat is its flywheel: more shoppers bring more sellers, more selection and more ad money, which pay for faster delivery and lower prices, which bring more shoppers. Its delivery network took decades and hundreds of billions to build.

pmLessons: A flywheel makes each part help the others; think in loops, not features.
Low prices plus fast delivery win trust, but ads can slowly erode it.
Subscriptions like Prime change behaviour: once people pay, they buy more.
Big bets can be undone: Amazon dropped Rufus in favour of Alexa for Shopping a year after launch.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of Alexa for Shopping?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define goals (conversion, satisfaction), pick a north star, add guardrails like ad revenue and returns.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Amazon raise the Prime price?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at churn risk, perks, competitors and value per member.

interviewQuestions.question: How do you compete with Temu?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment shoppers, look at Amazon Haul, speed and trust advantages.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain Amazon's flywheel.
interviewQuestions.hint: Selection, prices, experience, traffic, sellers; show how each feeds the next.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce fake reviews?
interviewQuestions.hint: Sources of fakes, detection, seller penalties, verified badges, metrics.
